name: Real estate appraiser temporary practice permit requirements by state: fee, duration, and per-year limit
description: Federal law (Title XI, 12 U.S.C. 3351(b)) requires every state to let a certified or licensed real estate appraiser from another state temporarily practice on a federally-related assignment, but each state's own appraiser board sets the fee, how long the permit lasts, and how many an appraiser can hold in a year -- and that procedural layer is set independently by each of the roughly 50 state boards, none of which cross-reference each other. Answers 'how do I get a temporary permit to appraise property in [state] if I'm licensed elsewhere', 'how many temporary permits can I get per year in [state]', 'how long is a temporary appraisal permit valid in [state]'. Matters to appraisers taking out-of-state assignments (disaster-area/CAT work, multi-state portfolio lenders, commercial appraisers) -- practicing without the specific state's permit is a licensing-board violation and can void the appraisal underlying the mortgage transaction. No consolidated free source was found; general 'appraiser reciprocity' guides online cover permanent reciprocal licensure, not the separate temporary-permit track, and none assemble it across states.
licence: Sources are state appraiser licensing boards, state administrative codes and state statutes -- government edicts, which carry no copyright, plus the boards' own procedural pages. We take the fact and a short attributed quote that links back, never a whole schedule. Six records cite Cornell's Legal Information Institute because the state's own host was unreachable or unquotable; LII is a republisher of the same uncopyrightable state rule text, and each of those six is annotated in sources.txt with the specific failure that forced it.

records.source_quote: A Temporary Practice Permit enables a certified or licensed appraiser in one state to obtain a temporary permit from another state to perform an appraisal assignment in the other state. The temporary permit is effective for one specific assignment or as listed on the client/appraiser contract or engagement letter. The appraiser is limited to five permits within a twelve-month period. If the assignment is not completed within six months, the appraiser must request an extension.

records.source_quote: An individual who is performing an appraisal on one assignment, for one client, in Tennessee may apply for a Temporary Practice Permit. Multiple properties can be considered as one assignment if the assignment is for the same client and reports are for the same intended use, and the same time period. There is a maximum of six (6) permits issued each calendar year; one extension may be requested in writing before the expiration date. According to Tennessee Code Annotated §62-39-338, the Commission may issue a temporary practice permit to a nonresident of this state who is properly licensed or certified in another state. The holder of a valid temporary practice permit shall be authorized to perform appraisals in this state, subject to the requirements of this chapter and the rules promulgated by the Commission. If a temporary practice permit holder’s out-of-state license has been revoked, suspended, denied renewal, or restricted, then the Commission may revoke, suspend, refuse to renew, or restrict a permit holder’s temporary practice permit. Requirements Licensing Requirements Consent to Service of Process List of each specific parcel of real property included in the assignment Application & Fees Complete the “Temporary Practice Permit” application online at <https://access.cloud.commerce.tn.gov/portal/public> core.tn.gov . The fee is $150 per temporary license permit.

records.source_quote: Temporary Registration Information An Appraiser who holds a current appraiser certificate in another state may use the titles described under Wis. Stat. § 458.055 when performing an appraisal in this state, if all of the following apply: • The appraisal is performed in a federally related transaction. • The appraiser’s practice in this state is practice of a temporary nature. • The appraiser completes the application and pays the fee specified in Wis. Stat. §§ 440.05(1) and (6). The term “practice of a temporary nature” is defined by the Department to mean the performance of one or more appraisals by an Appraiser conducted for purposes of completing a specific appraisal assignment.
